_about: The replacement naturalization or citizenship document (N-565, src/n565.py), per uscis.gov/n-565 (updated 06/01/2026) and the N-565 Instructions (02/27/25), read 10/02/2026: the G-28 and the N-565, then the Initial Evidence the Instructions list: a copy of a U.S. government photo ID; for a lost, stolen or destroyed certificate a copy of it (if available) and a police report and/or a sworn statement; for a mutilated one the document itself; for a name change the marriage certificate, decree or court order; for a wrong sex the birth certificate; for a new date of birth the court order or the government document. The original certificate goes in the envelope when the reason needs it (the packet shows a copy). The attorney approves titles and order.
title: Replacement certificate (N-565)
requires_message: The client hasn't been processed yet: process the client first.

handwork.text: The ORIGINAL certificate or declaration when the reason is a mutilated document, a USCIS error, a name change, a new date of birth or the sex at birth: it goes in the envelope, a copy stays in the file (N-565 Instructions, Initial Evidence).
A client who lives outside the U.S.: two identical color passport-style photos, name and A-Number lightly in pencil on the back. A client in the U.S. sends none.

exhibits.title: A copy of the client's U.S. government-issued photo ID (passport, driver's license or state ID)
The certificate or declaration: a copy of the lost one (if available), or the mutilated or incorrect one
A lost, stolen or destroyed certificate: the police report and/or the client's sworn statement
The evidence of a change: the marriage certificate, divorce or annulment decree, court order, or the birth certificate
